- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >40), model often overshoots downward in next 5–10 days; apply mild downward bias to forecast tail.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model delays correction; adjust forecast to reflect earlier sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion after strong upward moves; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast mean over 10-day horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model overfits to recent highs; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 7-day high unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates downward trend; apply 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to forecast mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative signals, model tends to ignore downward momentum; reduce forecast by 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
